title: The Divine Heart of God the Father: Consecration and Prayer to the Father
author: Anna V. (known as 'the Little Soul')
target_audience: Practicing Catholics and Christians seeking a deeper relationship with God the Father
Individuals interested in devotional practices and consecration
Readers devoted to Marian and Sacred Heart spiritual traditions
Those exploring contemporary Catholic mystical or private revelations
core_themes: Consecration and surrender to the Divine Will
Revelation of the compassionate, tender Heart of God the Father
The Father's desire for direct relationship with humanity
primary_purpose: To introduce and promote devotion to the Divine Heart of God the Father—an emerging devotion rooted in private revelations—by providing prayers, guidance on consecration, and explanations of the spiritual significance of honoring the Father's Heart.

structure_format.organization: Divided into sections with introductions, prayers, explanations, and instructions for consecration
features: Consecration prayers to God the Father
Reflections on the Father’s love and mercy
Excerpts from private revelations received by the author

key_concepts_lessons: God the Father desires to be known and loved distinctly, not only as part of the Trinity.
The Divine Heart of the Father is a source of infinite mercy, compassion, and protection.
Consecrating oneself to the Father’s Heart is a pathway to deeper union with God.
Prayers and trust in the Father can bring personal and communal spiritual transformation.
The Father’s Heart is both a new and ancient devotion responding to the needs of modern humanity.
notable_features: First English-language prayer of consecration to God the Father
Based on claimed private revelations to the author
Focus on distinct devotion to God the Father, not just Jesus or the Holy Spirit
Includes practical guidance for living out the devotion
cultural_historical_context: Published in 2012 in response to the growing interest in contemporary Catholic private revelations, the book addresses a perceived lack of direct devotion to God the Father within Catholic spirituality. It comes at a time when personal consecration and new devotions (such as Divine Mercy) have seen renewed popularity.
reception_impact: Niche following within Catholic mystical and devotional circles
Praised by devotees for deepening love and understanding of God the Father
Limited mainstream recognition due to its basis in private revelation
Some caution or skepticism among Catholic theologians regarding the ecclesiastical status of the devotion
comparable_titles: The Father Speaks to His Children by Mother Eugenia Ravasio
Consoling the Heart of Jesus by Michael Gaitley, MIC
Devotion to the Sacred Heart by John Croiset, SJ
33 Days to Morning Glory by Michael Gaitley, MIC
